iisg-bypass.pages.about.title: About the Bypass Project
iisg-bypass.pages.about.background.title: Background
iisg-bypass.pages.about.background.p1: The Bypass Project was a pilot initiative conducted by the Collections Processing department at the International Institute of Social History (IISH). The institute set out to experiment with the development of a digital infrastructure capable of facilitating secure access to IISH's born digital archives in their raw, unprocessed state.
iisg-bypass.pages.about.background.p2: With a non-operational born digital processing pipeline, unreliable structural and technical systems, and a catalogue with significant limitations in accessibility and discoverability, the project sought to develop an alternative access model — one that bypasses conventional archival workflows.
iisg-bypass.pages.about.approach.title: The Project Approach
iisg-bypass.pages.about.approach.p1: Informed by IISH researchers, a sample of unprocessed born digital archives was selected to serve as the basis for testing a processing pipeline developed by KNAW software developers. This pipeline utilizes forensic preservation tools and ElasticSearch to index the archives and construct a user interface incorporating file display functionality, in-text search, and metadata faceting.
iisg-bypass.pages.about.approach.p2: A virtual research environment (KASM) was designated as the secure access mechanism for the pilot archives, with defined security and privacy controls required as a condition of access. Due to the sensitive nature of these collections and ongoing privacy policy developments, access is currently restricted to IISH employees.
iisg-bypass.pages.about.collections.desc: Collections were selected based on their content, file type and level of sensitivity.
